ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Within the Caodong Five Ranks, arrival within integration (兼中到) is the fifth named relation. Dongshan’s verse places it outside the opposition of existence and nonexistence; later records repeatedly describe distinctions as exhausted or integrated.
EvidenceBody: Dongshan Liangjie begins the fifth-rank verse by saying it falls into neither existence nor nonexistence. Hongzhi Zhengjue gives it a dawn verse, while an unnamed monastic asks Fenyang Shanzhao for it and receives images of a weaving jade woman and a drumming stone man.

Langting Ting uses a returning cuckoo, Juelang Daosheng offers a later black-white diagram, Yongjue Yuanxian says affairs and principle are both gone, and Ruibai Mingxue applies it to a shout after holy and ordinary, subject and object, and existence and nonexistence are exhausted. These remain attributed illustrations of one rank.

Senses.Note: The exact label occurs 303 times in 95 allowlisted files. Seven witnesses in seven independent works support one fifth-rank relation.
